item.title: Russian ship attacked near Benghazi in suspected drone attack
item.description: Authorities in divided Libya's east said a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi port was hit on Sunday in a suspected drone attack, causing a blast but no casualties. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the front lines.

item.title: Israel’s Eisenkot slams ‘Jewish terrorism’ after attacks by settlers in West Bank
item.description: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday condemned arson attacks by settlers on Palestinian villages in the West Bank as “Jewish terrorism”. Israeli police said they opened an investigation into the attacks, which came nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister ⁠Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority.

item.title: Democrat Hubbard wins North Carolina recount, clinching historic House majority
item.description: Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the US House of Representatives from North Carolina on Sunday after defeating veteran Republican Virginia Foxx, who chairs the powerful House Rules Committee. His victory gave Democrats their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in the 2026 US midterms.

item.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
item.description: A Russian navy corvette docked at the Benghazi naval base ​in eastern Libya was hit on Sunday by a Ukrainian sea drone, according to local officials, hours before a cargo ship was also hit by a sea drone in a second attack. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday confirmed that his country's military was behind the strikes.

item.title: Burnham, 'Brejoin' & the Ghosts of Brexit
item.description:
“The people of Britain have spoken, and the answer is: we are out.”
The words of David Dimbleby at 4.40am on 24 June 2016, as the Brexit referendum result became clear.
But nearly a decade on, is Britain changing its mind?
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has reopened talks with Brussels, exploring options for a closer relationship with the EU. But the move has drawn criticism from key figures behind Brexit, including Theresa May and Boris Johnson.
So what is driving this rethink, and where might it lead?
France 24's Gavin Lee speaks to John McTernan, veteran Labour strategist and former adviser to Tony Blair.
